title: Artifacts for "A divisibility obstruction for joining two Moser lattices"
description:
Computational artifacts for the paper A divisibility obstruction for joining two Moser lattices.

Contains: eighteen DRAT proof certificates, all checked with drat-trim — eight for the paper's constructions and Parts' 509-vertex record, ten for the Galois-seam results around it; twenty witnesses for the periodic and empty-shell exclusions, each checked against its JSON by a validator that imports nothing from the project — the eleven periodic ones carry the lattice's unit steps, so properness is testable from the file, and --selftest corrupts a copy and shows it refused; exact coordinates for every graph, each file naming the field it was written in; and scripts/audit_numbers.py, which re-derives the paper's numbers from the definitions on the standard library alone and shares no code with the rest.

scripts/verify_all.sh runs all 47 recorded claims in parallel in about an hour, among them check_binding.py, which rebuilds every certified CNF from the shipped coordinates and compares bytes, and check_claims.py, which reads each number out of the manuscript and compares it with the filesystem. README.md opens with a coverage table saying, claim by claim, what the archive settles and what it does not. Neither drat-trim nor CaDiCaL is vendored: a checker obtained from the people whose proof you are checking is not a check.
notes: Code is MIT; the paper, the certificates and the data are CC BY 4.0. See LICENSES.md for the split and for the four files taken from arXiv:2010.12665, which are not ours to relicense.
